docs.text:
Nowcasts and forecasts of confirmed Bundibugyo virus disease cases for the BDBV Modeling Hub.

We build models to nowcast and forecast cases for the BDBV Modeling Hub. The hub collects weekly forecasts of the 2026 Bundibugyo virus disease outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo. Teams forecast confirmed cases by week of symptom onset for the country, its provinces and its health zones. Recent weeks are always incomplete because cases take time to be reported, so a nowcast estimates how many cases those weeks will finally hold.

We fine-tune a general-purpose forecasting model on simulated outbreaks so that it can nowcast and forecast cases from data that are still being reported. To judge whether fine-tuning helps, we compare it with simpler baselines: a standard nowcasting method with a random walk for forecasts, and the random walk on its own. We evaluate all of them on held-out simulations, on a German COVID-19 hospitalisation benchmark, and on the Ebola outbreak data. We describe this work in a paper.

We submit two of these models to the hub each week. One is the standard nowcasting method with its random walk. The other is the fine-tuned model, once it is switched on for submission.

We also fit renewal models, which describe how new infections arise from earlier ones. Our main renewal model takes its estimates of how fast the outbreak spreads from a larger model of the whole outbreak, BVDOutbreakSize. Two simpler versions, one without those estimates and one that fits each province on its own, show what each part adds. Each week we submit the first of the three that passes our checks, trying the main model first.

We also submit weekly estimates of the reproduction number, Rt, from the renewal model we submit that week, by week of infection. We do not recommend using them. They are estimated from cases by date of symptom onset, including the onsets the hub imputes, so they are likely to react late and be out of step with transmission. For Rt, we recommend our BVDOutbreakSize estimates instead.

We check every model by backtesting. We rerun each model on the data as they stood at past dates and score its forecasts against what was reported later. Every model is scored the same way, against the two random walk baselines, and compared with the other teams' forecasts. The baselines and the fine-tuned model are also scored on the German benchmark. The backtest, comparison with hub forecasts and German benchmark pages show the results.

docs.title: Getting started
docs.text:
git clone https://github.com/seabbs/bdbv-hub-modelling && cd bdbv-hub-modelling
uv sync                                        # every package
cp config/local.env.example config/local.env   # this machine's settings
task --list-all                                # every task

Then Getting started makes and scores forecasts in Python, and Setup covers the extras (PyRenew, torch, R) and a machine's settings. Each package below has a page or its own site, and a README on GitHub with how to install it, an example and its tasks.

docs.title: Quick links
docs.text:
The three projects:

  • Fine-tuned foundation

    Chronos-2 fine-tuned on simulated outbreaks to nowcast from reporting triangles, with its paper.

  • Joint-model-informed renewal

    Renewal models fitted on their own and informed by BVDOutbreakSize.

  • Hub submission

    The weekly submission to the BDBV Modeling Hub, its backtest and the comparison with the hub teams.

The packages they are built from:

Group Package What it is Shared nowcastutils Releases, snapshots, location hierarchies, the forecast task and sample trajectories. nowcasteval Scores, backtests and trajectory pairing. Models nowcastbaselines The random walk and the random walk nowcast, the baselines. nowcastfoundation Chronos-2 forecasts, the simulation grid and fine-tuning on simulated outbreaks. nowcastrenewal The renewal models and the joint model that simulates outbreaks. Studies bdbvhub The BDBV hub's data, the fit store, the hub file and the submission. nowcastbdbv The BDBV outbreak as a case study: the hub's data streams, health zones and delays. nowcastgermany The German COVID-19 hospitalisation nowcasting hub as a case study.

docs.title: Data credit
docs.text: Surveillance data: Institut National de Santé Publique (INSP) and the Incident Management Support Team (IMST), Democratic Republic of the Congo. Processed by ACCIDDA and the Kinshasa School of Public Health, University of Kinshasa, and distributed through the BDBV Modeling Hub.

docs.text:
Forecasts made at past vintages, scored on what each later release reported.

Fitted models' results come from the fit store, fitted at 21a6db4, 522bc5b.

docs.title: Overall
docs.text:
Scores on the complete weeks, or on what each later release reported, as picked (how scoring works, metrics). The models run here are scored on 1,000 draws per forecast ([samples] backtest in packages/nowcastbdbv/config/backtest.toml) and the stored fits on their 100 ([forecast] n_samples), with common random numbers. CRPS, log CRPS and the energy score use the fair estimators, so scores on different numbers of draws compare (scores). On later releases, the scores cover 15 origin and release pairs. The randomwalknowcast baseline has 6175 health zone forecasts. 2870 of them are of a place and week with no case, where every model's CRPS is close to 0, so mean CRPS is lower than over places with cases. The renewal models are not scored at health zones. Nationally and in the provinces, a complete week is scored on the first release cut off at least 35 days after it ends. Forecasts with such a release so far: 3240. Health zones are scored on the complete weeks of the latest release. The energy score scores each scale's places and weeks as one forecast per origin and release, so its \(n\) counts those.

  • renewal: 2 chains of 500 warm-up and 1500 draws, keeping 1 in 2, at a target acceptance of 0.9

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
Scores of the scored weeks, split by the type of place and by the plausibility flag of their forecast (checks). A place is silent with no case in the 9 weeks to the origin, small with at most 5 cases in any of those weeks, and larger otherwise. A forecast is flagged when its first week after the origin's latest full week drops to a third of the recent level (collapse) or rises far above every recent count (blow-up), and has no flag otherwise.

docs.title: Archived results
docs.text: Each submitted round has a GitHub release, round-<reference date>, at the commit it was submitted from. Once every stored fit at the round's hub release is of the current code, the Pages build adds every model's results to it: each model's forecast in the hub's format for the country, provinces and health zones, the scores, the fit summaries, the data and the rendered site. Zenodo archives each release with a DOI. The Zenodo copy holds the code only. The results are on the GitHub release.

docs.title: Citing the data
docs.text: The data come from the BDBV Modeling Hub. Credit them as the hub asks. The surveillance data are from the Institut National de Santé Publique (INSP) and the Incident Management Support Team (IMST), Democratic Republic of the Congo. They are processed by the Atlantic Coast Center for Infectious Disease Dynamics and Analytics (ACCIDDA) and the Kinshasa School of Public Health, University of Kinshasa.

docs.title: Comparison with hub forecasts
docs.text:
Our models and the forecasts submitted to the hub's weekly round, scored on the same data.

Fitted models' results come from the fit store, fitted at 21a6db4, 522bc5b.

Scores on the hub teams' cells only, the rounds, places and weeks any team forecast, on the weeks the latest release reports in full, from the release serving each round (how scoring works). A series marked submitted is the file we sent to a round, and one marked main build is the current main branch's forecast for every round, so a round we did not submit to shows only the main build. Each row's n is beside the hub cells scored in its round. Our models are scored on their 100 draws per forecast ([forecast] n_samples in packages/nowcastbdbv/config/backtest.toml) and the hub teams on their samples as submitted. CRPS, log CRPS and the energy score use the fair estimators, so scores on different numbers of draws compare (scores).

The static figures show our submitted series, the main builds of the models we submit and randomwalk above the hub teams. randomwalk and our other main builds, such as the 2026-11-07 renewal and renewalsp candidates, start switched off and can be switched on in the key.

The 2026-08-18 vintage has no delay data. The 2026-10-09 delay file exists only in the hub's git history.

The models leave out a first release that is a cumulative dump rather than part of the reporting: one whose next release comes more than \(D\) days later (nowcastutils.releases.cumulative_first_release). Every case it holds is older than \(D\) by the next release, so it records the counts to date, not how they were reported. The 2026-08-18 release is one, 50 days before the next cut-off, so every task from 2026-10-09 reads its releases from 2026-10-09 on. Forecasting starts at the first release with at least two usable releases up to it (nowcasteval.backtest.backtest_origins), so the first origin is 2026-10-17.

docs.title: Release cut-offs
docs.text:
Each release's cut-off is its latest onset day. It falls up to three days before the release date (days_to_release in the table above). The hub target is the sum of daily onsets over each epi week, Sunday to Saturday, so the week holding the cut-off is partial.

National daily onsets up to each release's cut-off, with each epi week's total (the hub target) above it and the release date dotted.

The last days before a cut-off hold few cases because most of their onsets are not yet reported. In the 2026-11-08 release, cut at 2026-11-05, the last five onset days hold 19, 19, 15, 10 and 5 cases. Its last week has five of seven days and 68 cases.

docs.title: National coherence
docs.text:
The national (CD) row should equal the sum of the provinces. The table counts the weeks where they differ, by vintage and stream.

Tables vintage observed weeks with a gap imputed weeks with a gap total weeks with a gap 2026-08-18 0 0 0 2026-10-09 0 0 0 2026-10-17 0 0 0 2026-10-24 0 0 0 2026-11-01 0 0 0 2026-11-08 0 0 0 2026-11-15 0 0 0 2026-11-22 0 0 0

A gap is cases counted nationally but in no province. The renewal fits stop on a gap and the submission's coherence check fails, since national is the sum of the provinces (supporting information).

docs.title: Target by vintage
docs.text: Weekly confirmed cases by onset week (observed plus imputed), by vintage.     Ituri and Nord Kivu hold most cases.

docs.title: Revisions of recent weeks
docs.text:
Each release is a vintage that restates every onset week, so a week's count grows as later releases report more of its cases.

Count for each recent onset week (labelled by the week's last day) in each release that reports it.

Nationally the week ending 2026-10-24 had 91 cases at the 2026-10-24 release, 381 at 2026-11-01 and 482 at 2026-11-08. The week ending 2026-10-31 rose from 150 to 349 in one release. Delay-file rows are the known-onset part of these counts, so their backfill follows the same pattern.

National counts in each vintage as a share of the latest vintage, by weeks from the onset week to the vintage's epi week. The last two weeks are far from complete. Weeks three back are still revised by 3 to 13%.

docs.title: Negative updates
docs.text:
A count falls when a release reports fewer cases for a place and onset week than the release before it. Each release is compared with the one before it, on the weeks of the earlier release with cases in either. A health zone missing from a release has no cases, so a zone that disappears counts as a fall to zero.

Share of place-weeks that fell (top) and cases removed as a share of all change (bottom), by the onset week's age at the earlier release. The 2026-08-18 to 2026-10-09 comparison spans seven weeks and the others one week. No national or province count fell while its onset week was less than three weeks old. Most falls came between the 2026-10-17 and 2026-10-24 releases, mainly in Nord Kivu.

Over all releases, 8 of 102 national weeks fell, 25 of 357 province weeks and 85 of 2738 health zone weeks. Falls removed 24 cases nationally against 2684 added, 1% of all change. They were 2% of all change for provinces and 4% for health zones. No fall was larger than 8 cases.

docs.title: Missing onsets
docs.text:
The hub publishes, for every vintage, the cases in each province and onset week with an imputed onset. How the hub imputes them, and how the renewal models model that, is in the paper's supporting information.

Imputed share of cases by onset week, by vintage. Point size grows with the week's count. It varies over time and between provinces. Share of all cases with an imputed onset in each release. Nationally it stays between 15% and 17%. In Nord Kivu it fell from 24% to 14% between the 2026-10-17 and 2026-10-24 releases, as cases gained an onset. Sud Ubangi's few cases all have an imputed onset.

The change between vintages approximates the cases reported without an onset. It is net of cases that gain an onset later, so it can be negative.

Cases added between vintages, by onset status. In Nord Kivu between 2026-10-17 and 2026-10-24, imputed onsets fell by 174 while known onsets rose by 379, so many cases gained an onset after their first report. A few delays are negative (down to −104 days) and a few very long (up to 193 days). The daily split into observed and imputed matches the weekly totals in every row, and the delay rows match the observed totals of their vintage.

Mean (line) and median (points) delay by onset week, with cases per week below on a log scale. Delays were long early on and shortened by June. The fall in the last weeks is right truncation, since only short delays have been reported yet.

docs.title: Health zones
docs.text: Health zone onsets are in data/daily_zones.csv.gz, and their weekly totals in data/health_zones.csv.gz, once task nowcastbdbv:data has fetched them. Zone totals sum to the province totals in every vintage. They set the zone series of the random walk baselines and the renewal models (see Health zones).

docs.title: German nowcast benchmark
docs.text:
Our models and the hub teams on the German COVID-19 hospitalisation nowcasting hub's data, scored as the hub scored them.

Nowcasts of the 7-day hospitalisation incidence by Meldedatum, made each day from 2021-11-22 to 2022-02-09 as in Wolffram et al. (2023)1, for the sums ending on every day from the nowcast date to 28 days before it, the hub's 29 targets. The paper's later dates, from 2022-02-10, are held out. Every nowcast is scored on its quantiles at the hub's seven levels, by WIS and the coverage of the 50% and 95% intervals, on the data reported 40 days after the sum ends (how the benchmark is set up). Relative scores are against randomwalknowcast on the nowcasts both made.

foundation are not shown: the German forecasts of their checkpoint (chronos-ft-3b95e171be2c) are not stored yet.

docs.title: Nowcasts
docs.text:
Each model's median and its 50% and 95% intervals at every seventh nowcast date, for Germany, each state and each age group. The solid line is the 7-day sum as reported 40 days after it ends, and the dashed line the data on the nowcast date. randomwalk and KIT-frozen_baseline start switched off; tick them to show them. The table under the plot scores the place and dates shown, so with all rounds it covers the plotted dates only.

Not yet available: our models' German nowcasts and scores come from the German benchmark (task nowcastgermany:benchmark), which the site does not run, and none are stored for it yet.

docs.text:
Data from the Robert Koch Institute (CC BY 4.0), processed by the German COVID-19 hospitalisation nowcasting hub, and the teams' nowcasts as the paper gathered them:

  • The reporting triangle: data-truth/COVID-19/COVID-19_hospitalizations.csv in KITmetricslab/hospitalization-nowcast-hub at 11c7453.

docs.title: Getting started¶
docs.text:
Forecast with two baselines, load the renewal model's stored fit at the same origin, then plot and score all three.

Every figure and table below comes from the Python code shown above it, which calls the package's functions directly. Setup installs the package and shows how to run this code in a REPL, a notebook or a script. task nowcastbdbv:data fetches the tidy data into data/, and task bdbvhub:fit-store fetches the stored renewal fits into output/fit-store. This page is a notebook, and task getting-started runs it again.

docs.title: Load the data¶
docs.text: load_target reads the weekly confirmed cases by onset week of every hub vintage. load_daily reads the daily onsets of every hub release, which the baselines need. load_delays reads the reporting delays the hub published, which the renewal models use.

docs.title: Build the forecast task¶
docs.text: The newest release scores the forecasts. The origin is the newest release before it at which the fit store holds a renewal fit, or the second newest release if it holds none. The task holds what a model sees at the origin, including the daily onsets of every release up to it, and the weeks to forecast. Its reference date is the Saturday after the origin, and the forecast weeks run from six weeks before it to four weeks after it. origin_tasks builds the task of every real origin as the fit store fits it, so the baselines and the stored renewal fit see the same task. current_keys gives the key of each renewal fit of this code and data, from the tasks with the health-zone tables (load_zone_data), as the store keys them. newest_fit returns the fit bdbvhub fit-store load uses at the newest origin that has one. That is the fit of the current key, or, until that fit is made, the newest fit of older code.

docs.title: Forecast with the baselines¶
docs.text: get_model returns a model from the registry by name. randomwalk carries the last complete week forward with random walk noise on the log scale. randomwalknowcast nowcasts the recent weeks first (Baseline models). randomwalknowcast is the baseline we submit to the hub as seabbs-rwnowcast. run_forecasts runs each model, checks the samples, adds the national total and returns 100 trajectories per location. learnt collects each model's modelled delay, which scoring uses.

docs.title: Fit the renewal model¶
docs.text:
The renewal model is fitted by MCMC (NUTS), which takes about half an hour, so this page does not fit it. The fit store fits it in CI at every real origin and stores the result. This is how it is fitted, with the sampler settings of the submission:

fitted = store.fit(
    "renewal", task, store.samplers(), store.code_digest("renewal")
)
store.write_fit("output/fit-store", fitted)

The page loads the stored fit instead.

docs.title: Load the stored renewal fit¶
docs.text: newest_fit read the fit chosen above into tables. Its forecasts table has the same columns as the baselines' forecasts, and its delays table holds the fit's modelled delay. If the store holds no renewal fit, the page says so and shows the baselines only.

docs.title: Plot the nowcast¶
docs.text: Recent weeks are still being reported, so the weeks before the reference date are nowcasts. The first figure keeps only those weeks, to show what the nowcast adds to the data at the origin. Each panel shows the data at the origin and as later reported, with the forecast fans (reading the figures). The panels are the national total and the three provinces with the most cases. save_light_dark writes a light and a dark version of each figure.

docs.title: Plot the forecast¶
docs.text: The second figure adds the reference week and the three forecast weeks.

docs.title: Score¶
docs.text: Each forecast is scored on what each later release reported (how scoring works). randomwalk is scored on its samples as they are, with no delay. release_backtest maps each other model's forecast of final counts to the counts a later release would report, using the model's own modelled delay. It scores the samples with the continuous ranked probability score (CRPS), on the counts and on the log scale, and interval coverage. The table gives each model's mean CRPS relative to randomwalknowcast, the site's baseline, for the national total and over the provinces.

docs.title: Next steps¶
docs.text: The API reference documents every function used here, grouped by task. The CLI page lists the commands the submission workflow runs. They fetch the data, run the backtest, forecast from the latest vintage and write the hub file.

docs.title: Delay and spread
docs.text:
The growth to final of each onset day by its age at the latest release, and the observation model by weeks back. A place using its parent's estimate is labelled with the parent. How both are fitted is in the paper's supporting information.

The renewal models fit the onset-to-report delay with the cases (supporting information). Each row is a place, the renewal models' shared delay first and then each place with a delay of its own. Each line is one model's fit at its latest origin. The left panel gives the share of onsets in the last week reported by each day since onset, with 90% intervals for the renewal models. It stops the day before the longest delay, where the model puts all later reports. The dashed line is randomwalknowcast's share reported by age at the same release, nationally for the shared delay. The right panel gives the renewal models' mean delay by onset week, with 90% intervals.

docs.title: Pairing sensitivity
docs.text:
How much pairing province draws within each week matters for randomwalk and randomwalknowcast (Correlated trajectories).

Each model forecasts each origin once, and its draws are scored with no pairing and paired by the rolling \(\rho_p\) estimated from its own errors, which is what it uses. Zones are not paired, so they are not compared here. Each week is paired on its own, so a place's sum over its weeks is not kept as one trajectory; it is shown, but nothing we submit or score uses it. Pairing only reorders draws, so each place's weekly forecast is unchanged; only sums and joint scores move. The country is the sum of the provinces (or Germany of its states), so its weekly score moves too. Values are mean sample CRPS (energy score for "all places and weeks") relative to no pairing, so below 1 is better, with the 90% interval coverage of the same targets.

docs.title: Paper
docs.text: A paper on fine-tuning Chronos-2 on simulated outbreaks for nowcasting. Its reference model is randomwalknowcast from nowcastbaselines, our JAX port of baselinenowcast with a random walk on top, which we develop as part of the paper. This page links to the rendered paper and to how it is reproduced.

docs.title: Where to start
docs.text:
• To read it, start with the main text, then the supporting information. Both have PDFs.
  • To reproduce it, start with Reproducing the paper: the workflow, its targets and how the held-out data are protected.
flowchart LR
  sim[Simulate] --> ft[Fine-tune] --> fc[Forecast] --> sc[Score] --> fig[Figures and tables] --> paper[Paper]
Reproduce it

From paper/:

task pipeline:dev      # the development run, without the held-out data
task pipeline:paper    # the paper run, with the held-out data
task render            # the paper as HTML and PDF from the last run

This site shows the development run. Figures from a study without its real data yet are marked as illustrative, dummy data.

Each step is a section of the workflow.
